question.problem: Within  the interval $[0,\pi ]$, determine the average value of $f(x)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.$
question.worked_solution:
Applying the average value formula, we find that the average value of the function is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{\text{avg}} & =\frac{1}{b-a}{\int }_{a}^{b}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi -0}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\pi }(2\operatorname{sin}⁡x-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\frac{1}{\pi }(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }[(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \pi ))-(-2\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot 0))] \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }[(-2\cdot (-1)+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1)-(-2\cdot 1+\frac{1}{2}\cdot 1)] \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }[(\frac{5}{2})-(-\frac{3}{2})] \\  & =\frac{1}{\pi }(4) \\  & =\frac{4}{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$
